# auth-service commands

This page lists every `auth-service` command with its arguments and options. It
is generated from the same definitions as `auth-service --help`, so `--help` on
any command prints the same text. [Administration](administration.md) shows the
commands at work, and [deploying](deploying.md#running-auth-service-commands)
how to run them in an environment.

Every command also accepts `-h` and `--help`.

## `auth-service`

Piquel authentication service. Runs `serve` when no command is given.

```text
auth-service [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

Commands:

- [`auth-service serve`](#auth-service-serve): Serve the authentication service.
- [`auth-service migrate`](#auth-service-migrate): Apply database migrations. Connected as the schema owner, also create or reset the role other commands connect as.
- [`auth-service keys`](#auth-service-keys): Inspect, rotate, revoke and import signing keys, check token digest keys, and print the audit key's verifier key. Every replica picks up a signing key change within a minute.
- [`auth-service user`](#auth-service-user): Search, show, disable, reactivate and recover accounts.
- [`auth-service session`](#auth-service-session): End an account's sessions.
- [`auth-service invite`](#auth-service-invite): Create, list and revoke signup invitations.
- [`auth-service client`](#auth-service-client): Register, inspect and change OIDC clients. Changes apply to the next request.
- [`auth-service audit`](#auth-service-audit): Page through, verify and prune the audit history.
- [`auth-service admin`](#auth-service-admin): Grant, revoke or list administrators.
- [`auth-service handle`](#auth-service-handle): Check accounts against the handle rules, and change their handles.
- [`auth-service deliveries`](#auth-service-deliveries): Inspect, retry and cancel outbound deliveries.
- [`auth-service announcement`](#auth-service-announcement): Draft, send and read announcements to accounts, such as a security incident or a change to the privacy policy.
- [`auth-service account`](#auth-service-account): Read or change one account's settings on its owner's behalf.

## `auth-service serve`

Serve the authentication service.

```text
auth-service serve [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service migrate`

Apply database migrations. Connected as the schema owner, also create or reset the role other commands connect as.

```text
auth-service migrate [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service keys`

Inspect, rotate, revoke and import signing keys, check token digest keys, and print the audit key's verifier key. Every replica picks up a signing key change within a minute.

```text
auth-service keys [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

Commands:

- [`auth-service keys list`](#auth-service-keys-list): List signing keys with their state and dates, oldest first.
- [`auth-service keys rotate`](#auth-service-keys-rotate): Publish a new signing key, which signs after 24 hours. Prints its ID.
- [`auth-service keys revoke`](#auth-service-keys-revoke): Delete a signing key at once, e.g. a compromised one. When it was the active key, the `next` and `retiring` keys go with it, since their private keys were stored alongside, and a new one signs at once. Verifiers that cached it keep accepting it until their cache expires, up to an hour.
- [`auth-service keys digest-usage`](#auth-service-keys-digest-usage): Count stored token digests per token digest key, to tell when `AUTH_TOKEN_DIGEST_KEY_ACCEPTED` can be removed.
- [`auth-service keys import`](#auth-service-keys-import): Import the deployment's PEM signing key as the active key, so tokens it signed keep verifying. Does nothing unless the key set is empty.
- [`auth-service keys audit`](#auth-service-keys-audit): Print the verifier key of the audit key `AUTH_AUDIT_KEY_PROVIDER` names, for `AUTH_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`'s host, to commit to docs/dev/security/audit-key.pub.

## `auth-service keys list`

List signing keys with their state and dates, oldest first.

```text
auth-service keys list [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service keys rotate`

Publish a new signing key, which signs after 24 hours. Prints its ID.

```text
auth-service keys rotate [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--now`: Sign with it at once, skipping pre-publication: verifiers that cached the previous key set reject its tokens until they fetch keys again. Asks first.
- `--yes`: Do not ask for confirmation. Required when standard input is not a terminal.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service keys revoke`

Delete a signing key at once, e.g. a compromised one. When it was the active key, the `next` and `retiring` keys go with it, since their private keys were stored alongside, and a new one signs at once. Verifiers that cached it keep accepting it until their cache expires, up to an hour.

```text
auth-service keys revoke [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`: The key's ID.

Options:

- `--yes`: Do not ask for confirmation. Required when standard input is not a terminal.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service keys digest-usage`

Count stored token digests per token digest key, to tell when `AUTH_TOKEN_DIGEST_KEY_ACCEPTED` can be removed.

```text
auth-service keys digest-usage [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service keys import`

Import the deployment's PEM signing key as the active key, so tokens it signed keep verifying. Does nothing unless the key set is empty.

```text
auth-service keys import [OPTIONS] <REFERENCE>
```

Arguments:

- `<REFERENCE>`: The PEM key, at `file://PATH` or `env://NAME`.

Options:

- `--id <ID>`: The key's ID, as tokens it signed name it. Default: `primary`.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service keys audit`

Print the verifier key of the audit key `AUTH_AUDIT_KEY_PROVIDER` names, for `AUTH_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`'s host, to commit to docs/dev/security/audit-key.pub.

```text
auth-service keys audit [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service user`

Search, show, disable, reactivate and recover accounts.

```text
auth-service user [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

Commands:

- [`auth-service user search`](#auth-service-user-search): Search accounts by ID, or by part of a handle, display name or email, ignoring case. Lists 50 at a time, by handle.
- [`auth-service user show`](#auth-service-user-show): Show an account's profile, status, emails, passkeys, linked identities, sessions and consents. Recorded, since it shows personal data.
- [`auth-service user disable`](#auth-service-user-disable): Disable an account and end its sessions and refresh tokens. Never the last active administrator's.
- [`auth-service user enable`](#auth-service-user-enable): Let a disabled account sign in again.
- [`auth-service user recover`](#auth-service-user-recover): Recover an account whose owner lost every passkey.
- [`auth-service user delete`](#auth-service-user-delete): Schedule an active account's deletion: it can no longer sign in, its sessions end, and it is purged after 30 days unless restored first. Never the last active administrator's.
- [`auth-service user undo-recovery`](#auth-service-user-undo-recovery): Undo an account's recovery for its owner, once they are confirmed.
- [`auth-service user restore`](#auth-service-user-restore): Restore an account scheduled for deletion, so it can sign in again.

## `auth-service user search`

Search accounts by ID, or by part of a handle, display name or email, ignoring case. Lists 50 at a time, by handle.

```text
auth-service user search [OPTIONS] [QUERY]
```

Arguments:

- `[QUERY]`: What to look for. Lists every account when empty.

Options:

- `--page <PAGE>`: The page to list, counting from 1.
- `--output <OUTPUT>`: A table for people, or JSON for scripts. Default: `table`. Values: `table` (Tab-separated lines for people), `json` (The view the admin dashboard shows, as JSON, for scripts: its shape is `piquel_common::admin`'s).
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service user show`

Show an account's profile, status, emails, passkeys, linked identities, sessions and consents. Recorded, since it shows personal data.

```text
auth-service user show [OPTIONS] <USER>
```

Arguments:

- `<USER>`: The account: its handle, ID or verified email.

Options:

- `--output <OUTPUT>`: A table for people, or JSON for scripts. Default: `table`. Values: `table` (Tab-separated lines for people), `json` (The view the admin dashboard shows, as JSON, for scripts: its shape is `piquel_common::admin`'s).
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service user disable`

Disable an account and end its sessions and refresh tokens. Never the last active administrator's.

```text
auth-service user disable [OPTIONS] --reason <REASON> <USER>
```

Arguments:

- `<USER>`: The account: its handle, ID or verified email.

Options:

- `--reason <REASON>`: Why, kept with the event as personal data: 1 to 500 characters. Required.
- `--yes`: Do not ask for confirmation. Required when standard input is not a terminal.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service user enable`

Let a disabled account sign in again.


Arguments:

- `<USER>`: The account: its handle, ID or verified email.

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service user recover`

Recover an account whose owner lost every passkey.

First lists the account's recoveries that started, ended or were used within a probation's length. Refuses while one is in probation: find out who used it, and undo it with `user undo-recovery` first. An unused link is replaced. Refuses an administrator's account: revoke its rights first. Ends the account's sessions, removes its unverified addresses, and sends its primary verified address a link that enrolls one passkey, within a day; prints the link too, for when there is none. Through the probation that follows, that passkey signs in but confirms no change, and any older passkey can undo the recovery. Needs `AUTH_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` and the token digest key, which derives the link.

```text
auth-service user recover [OPTIONS] --reason <REASON> <USER>
```

Arguments:

- `<USER>`: The account: its handle, ID or verified email.

Options:

- `--reason <REASON>`: Why, recorded with the recovery and shown to the owner, and to whoever uses the link, in the history: what was asked, never the evidence. 1 to 500 characters. Required.
- `--revoke`: The account was in someone else's hands: also revoke every passkey not kept with `--keep`, the last included, unlink every social identity and withdraw every consent. The link is then only printed, and every verified address is told at once. Remove the addresses the owner does not recognize afterwards, before handing the link over.
- `--keep <KEEP>`: With `--revoke`, a passkey the owner vouches for, which stays and can still undo the recovery. Repeatable.
- `--yes`: Do not ask for confirmation. Required when standard input is not a terminal.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service user delete`

Schedule an active account's deletion: it can no longer sign in, its sessions end, and it is purged after 30 days unless restored first. Never the last active administrator's.

```text
auth-service user delete [OPTIONS] --reason <REASON> <USER>
```

Arguments:

- `<USER>`: The account: its handle, ID or verified email.

Options:

- `--reason <REASON>`: Why, kept with the event as personal data: 1 to 500 characters. Required.
- `--immediately`: Purge the account now, in any status, without a grace period. This cannot be undone.
- `--yes`: Do not ask for confirmation. Required when standard input is not a terminal.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service user undo-recovery`

Undo an account's recovery for its owner, once they are confirmed.

For an owner with no passkey left from before it, or whose account is disabled. In probation, removes its passkey, even the last, withdraws every consent, and ends every session and refresh grant; its link unused, cancels the link.

```text
auth-service user undo-recovery [OPTIONS] --reason <REASON> <USER>
```

Arguments:

- `<USER>`: The account: its handle, ID or verified email.

Options:

- `--reason <REASON>`: Why, recorded with each change and shown to the owner in their history: 1 to 500 characters. Required.
- `--yes`: Do not ask for confirmation. Required when standard input is not a terminal.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service user restore`

## `auth-service client`

Register, inspect and change OIDC clients. Changes apply to the next request.

```text
auth-service client [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

Commands:

- [`auth-service client create`](#auth-service-client-create): Register a client. A confidential client's secret is printed once.
- [`auth-service client apply`](#auth-service-client-apply): Register a client, or update it to match, with the secret its deployment generated: for clients a deployment manages, such as the admin dashboard. Records nothing when the client already matches.
- [`auth-service client list`](#auth-service-client-list): List every client, deleted ones included.
- [`auth-service client show`](#auth-service-client-show): Print a client's registration and its secrets' lifetimes as JSON.
- [`auth-service client update`](#auth-service-client-update): Change a client's registration; what is not given keeps its value.
- [`auth-service client disable`](#auth-service-client-disable): Stop a client from authorizing, exchanging codes and refreshing tokens.
- [`auth-service client delete`](#auth-service-client-delete): Delete a client: it stops working at once, its refresh tokens, secrets and consents go, and its ID can never be registered again.
- [`auth-service client enable`](#auth-service-client-enable): Let a disabled client work again.
- [`auth-service client suspend`](#auth-service-client-suspend): Block a client: it is disabled, and its owner cannot enable it again until `unsuspend`.
- [`auth-service client unsuspend`](#auth-service-client-unsuspend): Lift a client's suspension. It stays disabled until enabled.
- [`auth-service client rotate-secret`](#auth-service-client-rotate-secret): Print a new secret for a confidential client. Earlier secrets keep working during the grace period, while the client switches to the new one.
- [`auth-service client origin`](#auth-service-client-origin): Approve, remove or list the origins whose pages may sign users in with their passkeys, without sending them to auth's pages.

## `auth-service client create`

Register a client. A confidential client's secret is printed once.

```text
auth-service client create [OPTIONS] --name <NAME> --redirect-uri <REDIRECT_URIS> <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`: The client's ID: 1 to 64 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-'.

Options:

- `--name <NAME>`: The name consent screens show. Required.
- `--redirect-uri <REDIRECT_URIS>`: An authorization callback, matched exactly; repeat for several. Required.
- `--post-logout-uri <POST_LOGOUT_URIS>`: A page the browser may return to after logout; repeat for several.
- `--scope <SCOPES>`: A scope the client may request; repeat for several. Defaults to openid, profile and email.
- `--confidential`: The client runs on a server and authenticates with a secret.
- `--refresh`: The client may receive refresh tokens when it requests `offline_access`.
- `--trusted`: The client skips the consent screen. Only for first-party clients.
- `--require-par`: The client must push its authorization requests (RFC 9126), so none of their parameters travel through the browser.
- `--backchannel-logout-uri <BACKCHANNEL_LOGOUT_URI>`: Where auth posts a logout token when a session the client holds tokens from ends (OIDC Back-Channel Logout); HTTPS with a public address.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service client apply`

Register a client, or update it to match, with the secret its deployment generated: for clients a deployment manages, such as the admin dashboard. Records nothing when the client already matches.

```text
auth-service client apply [OPTIONS] --name <NAME> --redirect-uri <REDIRECT_URIS> <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`: The client's ID: 1 to 64 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-'.

Options:

- `--name <NAME>`: The name consent screens show. Required.
- `--redirect-uri <REDIRECT_URIS>`: An authorization callback, matched exactly; repeat for several. Required.
- `--post-logout-uri <POST_LOGOUT_URIS>`: A page the browser may return to after logout; repeat for several.
- `--scope <SCOPES>`: A scope the client may request; repeat for several. Defaults to openid, profile and email.
- `--confidential`: The client runs on a server and authenticates with a secret.
- `--refresh`: The client may receive refresh tokens when it requests `offline_access`.
- `--trusted`: The client skips the consent screen. Only for first-party clients.
- `--require-par`: The client must push its authorization requests (RFC 9126), so none of their parameters travel through the browser.
- `--backchannel-logout-uri <BACKCHANNEL_LOGOUT_URI>`: Where auth posts a logout token when a session the client holds tokens from ends (OIDC Back-Channel Logout); HTTPS with a public address.
- `--secret <REFERENCE>`: A confidential client's secret, at `file://PATH` or `env://NAME`: 32 random bytes in unpadded base64url, generated by its deployment. Never printed.
- `--grace <GRACE>`: How long earlier secrets keep working once the secret changes, so the running deployment keeps signing in until it rolls out. Default: `1h`.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service client update`

Change a client's registration; what is not given keeps its value.

```text
auth-service client update [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`: The client's ID.

Options:

- `--name <NAME>`: A new name for consent screens.
- `--add-redirect-uri <ADD_REDIRECT_URIS>`: An authorization callback to add; repeat for several.
- `--remove-redirect-uri <REMOVE_REDIRECT_URIS>`: An authorization callback to remove, exactly as registered; repeat for several.
- `--add-post-logout-uri <ADD_POST_LOGOUT_URIS>`: A post-logout page to add; repeat for several.
- `--remove-post-logout-uri <REMOVE_POST_LOGOUT_URIS>`: A post-logout page to remove, exactly as registered; repeat for several.
- `--scope <SCOPES>`: Replaces the scopes the client may request; repeat for several.
- `--refresh`: Allow refresh tokens.
- `--no-refresh`: Stop issuing refresh tokens; existing ones stop working.
- `--trusted`: Skip the consent screen.
- `--untrusted`: Show the consent screen again.
- `--require-par`: Require pushed authorization requests.
- `--no-require-par`: Accept authorization requests sent through the browser again.
- `--backchannel-logout-uri <BACKCHANNEL_LOGOUT_URI>`: Post logout tokens to this URI instead.
- `--no-backchannel-logout-uri`: Stop posting logout tokens to the client.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service client suspend`

Block a client: it is disabled, and its owner cannot enable it again until `unsuspend`.

```text
auth-service client suspend [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`: The client's ID.

Options:

- `--yes`: Do not ask for confirmation. Required when standard input is not a terminal.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service client unsuspend`

Lift a client's suspension. It stays disabled until enabled.

```text
auth-service client unsuspend [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`: The client's ID.

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service client rotate-secret`

Print a new secret for a confidential client. Earlier secrets keep working during the grace period, while the client switches to the new one.

```text
auth-service client rotate-secret [OPTIONS] <ID>
```

Arguments:

- `<ID>`: The client's ID.

Options:

- `--grace <GRACE>`: How long earlier secrets keep working, e.g. 30m, 24h or 7d; 0 revokes them now, which asks first. Default: `24h`.
- `--yes`: Do not ask for confirmation. Required when standard input is not a terminal.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service client origin`

Approve, remove or list the origins whose pages may sign users in with their passkeys, without sending them to auth's pages.

```text
auth-service client origin [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

Commands:

- [`auth-service client origin add`](#auth-service-client-origin-add): Approve an origin. The client must be trusted and have a redirect URI on it, and approved origins may span at most 5 domains, as browsers honour.
- [`auth-service client origin remove`](#auth-service-client-origin-remove): Remove an origin: its pages stop signing users in.
- [`auth-service client origin list`](#auth-service-client-origin-list): List every approved origin.

## `auth-service client origin add`

Approve an origin. The client must be trusted and have a redirect URI on it, and approved origins may span at most 5 domains, as browsers honour.

- `<ID>`: The client's ID.

## `auth-service audit`

Page through, verify and prune the audit history.

```text
auth-service audit [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

Commands:

- [`auth-service audit list`](#auth-service-audit-list): Page through recorded events, newest first.
- [`auth-service audit verify`](#auth-service-audit-verify): Recompute the chain and check every checkpoint against it, and record what it found, which the dashboard's Audit tab shows. Exits non-zero, naming the first position that does not match, when the chain is broken.
- [`auth-service audit prune`](#auth-service-audit-prune): Delete the events through a checkpoint, once the chain verifies through it. The checkpoint becomes the anchor the remaining chain extends. Connects as the schema owner when `AUTH_DATABASE_OWNER_URL` is set: auth's own role may not delete events.

## `auth-service audit list`

Page through recorded events, newest first.

```text
auth-service audit list [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--user <USER>`: Only events concerning this account: its handle, ID or verified email.
- `--kind <KIND>`: Only events of this kind, e.g. `session_revoked`.
- `--views`: List administrators' and operators' views of accounts too, which are left out unless `--kind account_viewed` asks for them.
- `--page <PAGE>`: The page to list, counting from 1 at the newest events.
- `--output <OUTPUT>`: A table for people, or JSON for scripts. Default: `table`. Values: `table` (Tab-separated lines for people), `json` (The view the admin dashboard shows, as JSON, for scripts: its shape is `piquel_common::admin`'s).
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service audit verify`

Recompute the chain and check every checkpoint against it, and record what it found, which the dashboard's Audit tab shows. Exits non-zero, naming the first position that does not match, when the chain is broken.

```text
auth-service audit verify [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--key <KEY>`: A file of verifier keys, one per line, to use instead of the keys committed to the repository for `AUTH_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`'s host, e.g. a preview's, as `keys audit` prints it.
- `--output <OUTPUT>`: A table for people, or JSON for scripts. Default: `table`. Values: `table` (Tab-separated lines for people), `json` (The view the admin dashboard shows, as JSON, for scripts: its shape is `piquel_common::admin`'s).
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service audit prune`

Delete the events through a checkpoint, once the chain verifies through it. The checkpoint becomes the anchor the remaining chain extends. Connects as the schema owner when `AUTH_DATABASE_OWNER_URL` is set: auth's own role may not delete events.

```text
auth-service audit prune [OPTIONS] --through <THROUGH>
```

Options:

- `--through <THROUGH>`: The position of the checkpoint to prune through. Required.
- `--key <KEY>`: A file of verifier keys, one per line, to use instead of the keys committed to the repository for `AUTH_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`'s host, e.g. a preview's, as `keys audit` prints it.
- `--yes`: Do not ask for confirmation. Required when standard input is not a terminal.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service admin`

Grant, revoke or list administrators.

Commands:

## `auth-service admin grant`

Make an active account an administrator.

Refuses while a recovery of the account can still be undone: granted during its probation, the rights would go live for whoever used its link once it settles.

```text
auth-service admin grant [OPTIONS] <USER>
```

Arguments:

- `<USER>`: The account: its handle, ID or verified email.

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service admin revoke`

Remove an account's administrator rights. The last active administrator keeps theirs.

```text
auth-service admin revoke [OPTIONS] <USER>
```

Arguments:

- `<USER>`: The account: its handle, ID or verified email.

Options:

- `--yes`: Do not ask for confirmation. Required when standard input is not a terminal.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service admin list`

List administrators, oldest grant first.

```text
auth-service admin list [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--output <OUTPUT>`: A table for people, or JSON for scripts. Default: `table`. Values: `table` (Tab-separated lines for people), `json` (The view the admin dashboard shows, as JSON, for scripts: its shape is `piquel_common::admin`'s).
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service handle`

Check accounts against the handle rules, and change their handles.

```text
auth-service handle [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

Commands:

- [`auth-service handle check`](#auth-service-handle-check): List accounts whose handle is reserved.
- [`auth-service handle rename`](#auth-service-handle-rename): Give an account a new handle, without the settings cooldown, and record the change.
- [`auth-service handle release`](#auth-service-handle-release): Delete a released handle, or a purged account's last one, so anyone may claim it again, e.g. after a trademark dispute. An account's current handle is never released: rename the account first. Asks first.
- [`auth-service handle released`](#auth-service-handle-released): List released handles and purged accounts' last ones, which `release` frees.
- [`auth-service handle reserved`](#auth-service-handle-reserved): List the handles administrators reserved, then the built-in reserved names.
- [`auth-service handle reserve`](#auth-service-handle-reserve): Reserve a handle: signup and the settings refuse it and its look-alikes until an administrator gives it with `rename --allow-reserved`, or `unreserve`s it.
- [`auth-service handle unreserve`](#auth-service-handle-unreserve): Remove a handle from the reserved list, so anyone may claim it again.

## `auth-service handle check`

List accounts whose handle is reserved.

```text
auth-service handle check [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service handle rename`

Give an account a new handle, without the settings cooldown, and record the change.

```text
auth-service handle rename [OPTIONS] --reason <REASON> <USER> <NEW>
```

Arguments:

- `<USER>`: The account: its current handle, ID or verified email.
- `<NEW>`: Its new handle.

Options:

- `--reason <REASON>`: Why, kept with the event as personal data: 1 to 500 characters. Required.
- `--allow-reserved`: Allow a reserved name, or one that looks like it.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service handle release`

Delete a released handle, or a purged account's last one, so anyone may claim it again, e.g. after a trademark dispute. An account's current handle is never released: rename the account first. Asks first.

```text
auth-service handle release [OPTIONS] <HANDLE>
```

Arguments:

- `<HANDLE>`: The released handle.

Options:

- `--yes`: Do not ask for confirmation. Required when standard input is not a terminal.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service announcement`

Draft, send and read announcements to accounts, such as a security incident or a change to the privacy policy.

```text
auth-service announcement [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

Commands:

- [`auth-service announcement show`](#auth-service-announcement-show): Show an announcement: its text, whom it goes to, how many of them its email reaches, and once sent, how its emails fared.
- [`auth-service announcement draft`](#auth-service-announcement-draft): Draft an announcement, and print its ID. Nothing is sent yet.
- [`auth-service announcement edit`](#auth-service-announcement-edit): Replace a draft's subject, text and recipients.
- [`auth-service announcement discard`](#auth-service-announcement-discard): Delete a draft.

```text

```

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.


Options:

- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service announcement draft`

Draft an announcement, and print its ID. Nothing is sent yet.

```text
auth-service announcement draft [OPTIONS] --subject <SUBJECT> --body-file <BODY_FILE>
```

Options:

- `--subject <SUBJECT>`: The email's subject: one line of up to 150 characters. Required.
- `--body-file <BODY_FILE>`: The file holding the text, or `-` for standard input: up to 20,000 characters, paragraphs separated by blank lines. The email starts with "Hello," and ends with "Piquel". Required.
- `--everyone`: Send it to every account, as of its sending.
- `--to <TO>`: Send it to this account, by handle, ID or verified email. Repeat for up to 1,000 accounts.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.

## `auth-service announcement edit`

```text

```

- `<ID>`: The draft's ID.

Options:

- `--subject <SUBJECT>`: The email's subject: one line of up to 150 characters. Required.
- `--body-file <BODY_FILE>`: The file holding the text, or `-` for standard input: up to 20,000 characters, paragraphs separated by blank lines. The email starts with "Hello," and ends with "Piquel". Required.
- `--everyone`: Send it to every account, as of its sending.
- `--to <TO>`: Send it to this account, by handle, ID or verified email. Repeat for up to 1,000 accounts.
- `--operator <NAME>`: Who runs the command, as its events record them, such as your handle. Defaults to `AUTH_OPERATOR`, then `$USER`; administrative commands need one.
